original_question: How do the sums of the Betti numbers for ΛTM and Ω(T (p, q) grow as T → ∞?
target_in_paper: Question 3.1.1 (Paternain) in §3.1, “Sums of the Betti numbers,” with notation supplied from §1. pp. 1 and 5. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already aimed at the exact target in the paper: it asks about the asymptotic growth, as T → ∞, of the sums of the Betti numbers for the two truncated spaces Λ^T M and Ω^T(p,q). That is essentially the first sentence of Question 3.1.1, except for a notation typo in Ω^T(p,q). ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
missing_details: The ambient setting is omitted: the paper states the question for points p,q in a Riemannian manifold M. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))

The notation should be Ω^T(p,q), not “Ω(T (p, q)”. In §1, Ω(p,q) is the space of piecewise smooth paths from p to q, and Ω^T(p,q) is its subspace of paths of length at most T. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))

ΛM should be identified as the free loop space of piecewise smooth maps S^1 → M, and Λ^T M as the subspace of loops of length ≤ T. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
The draft omits the second sentence of the official question: “Does the growth depend on the metric?” ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))

To make the question stand-alone, “the sums of the Betti numbers” should be written explicitly as the total Betti numbers ∑_i b_i(Λ^T M) and ∑_i b_i(Ω^T(p,q)). The paper leaves coefficients implicit, so a stand-alone version should either keep “Betti numbers” in that standard sense or explicitly fix coefficients. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))

The nearby context also records that for each fixed T, Ω^T(p,q) has the homotopy type of a finite complex, hence finite total Betti number, and that the same is true for Λ^T M; this finiteness premise is implicit in the draft. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
refined_question: Let (M,g) be a Riemannian manifold, let p,q ∈ M, let ΛM be the free loop space of piecewise smooth maps S^1 → M, and let Λ^T M ⊂ ΛM be the subspace of loops of length at most T. Likewise, let Ω(p,q) be the space of piecewise smooth paths from p to q, and let Ω^T(p,q) ⊂ Ω(p,q) be the subspace of paths of length at most T. As T → ∞, how do the total Betti numbers ∑_i b_i(Λ^T M) and ∑_i b_i(Ω^T(p,q)) grow? In particular, does this growth depend on the Riemannian metric g? ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
justification: The draft is trying to capture Question 3.1.1 (Paternain) in §3.1, not a broader neighboring problem. The paper’s §1 introduces exactly the notations ΛM, Λ^T M, Ω(p,q), and Ω^T(p,q), together with the piecewise-smooth and length-truncation conventions. Immediately before Question 3.1.1, §3.1 states that Ω^T(p,q) has the homotopy type of a finite complex and therefore finite total Betti number for each T, and that the same is true for Λ^T M. The official question then asks both about the growth of those sums as T → ∞ and whether that growth depends on the metric. No equivalent reformulation is stated nearby, so the sharpest faithful rewrite is simply a self-contained restatement of Question 3.1.1 with the notation unpacked. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
